nodes.summary: For a longest-path instance with vertex count $n$ and edge list $E$, its graph is the graph of the edge list $E$ on $n$ vertices: the simple graph on $\{0, \dots, n - 1\}$ in which distinct vertices $i$ and $j$ are adjacent when $(i, j)$ or $(j, i)$ belongs to $E$.
nodes.title: Graph of a longest-path instance

nodes.summary: LONGEST PATH is the decision problem that accepts a bitstring $x$ exactly when $x$ decodes, under the canonical bitstring encoding, to a longest-path instance $(n, E, K, s, t)$ that is well formed and in which the graph of $E$ on $n$ vertices has a simple path from $s$ to $t$ with at least $K$ edges. Bitstrings that do not decode to a longest-path instance are rejected.
nodes.title: The LONGEST PATH decision problem

nodes.summary: A longest-path instance $(n, E, K, s, t)$ is feasible when the graph of $E$ on $n$ vertices has a simple path from $s$ to $t$ with at least $K$ edges, that is, a list $v_0, \dots, v_m$ of pairwise distinct vertices with $m \ge K$, $v_0 = s$ and $v_m = t$, in which $v_j$ and $v_{j+1}$ are adjacent for every $j < m$.
nodes.title: Feasibility of a longest-path instance

nodes.summary: A longest-path instance is a tuple $(n, E, K, s, t)$ consisting of a natural number $n$, the number of vertices; a list $E$ of pairs of natural numbers, the edges; and natural numbers $K$, the length bound, $s$, the start vertex, and $t$, the target vertex.
nodes.title: Longest-path instances

nodes.summary: The LONGEST PATH decision problem belongs to NP, and every decision problem in NP has a polynomial-time many-one reduction to LONGEST PATH.
nodes.title: LONGEST PATH is NP-complete

nodes.summary: A longest-path instance $(n, E, K, s, t)$ is well formed when $s < n$, $t < n$, the list $E$ has no repeated entries, and every pair $(u, v)$ in $E$ satisfies $u < n$, $v < n$ and $u \ne v$, and its reverse $(v, u)$ does not belong to $E$.
nodes.title: Well-formed longest-path instances

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
